newsitem.title: USA: Kinko's cuts prices for American passengers.
newsitem.headline: Kinko's cuts prices for American passengers.

text.p: Kinko's Inc said Thursday it has cut videoconference prices by 50 percent for passengers of AMR Corp's American Airlines who may be stranded from their loved ones or business associates by a possible strike by American pilots.

The business services retail store said the half price offer will be available to stranded American ticket holders from the date of the airline ticket departure, through to the date of the scheduled return.
"Videoconferencing is the perfect solution to those strike-stranded travelers concerned about missing an important meeting," says Laura McCormick, spokeswoman for Kinko's.
Kinko's said it has videoconference facilities in areas expected to be hardest hit by the potential strike, including American hub cities of Dallas/Ft. Worth, Chicago and Miami.
Videoconference at Kinko's is normally $150 per location, per hour, Monday through Thursday dropping to $75 on Friday, Saturday and Sunday.
American Airline ticket holders will be charged $75 per location per hour Monday through Sunday. The lower prices will apply until April 30 or until the strike ends, whichever comes first.
